thread:
alex: quick heads-up — i ran `terraform plan` in staging (workspace=staging) and it wants to recreate an ElastiCache parameter group and replace the redis cluster; also shows a tainted aws_db_instance for the reports db. i didn't touch those resources.

maria: which backend? remote S3? any lock messages?

alex: remote state in s3/dynamo. no lock active when i ran it. plan output snippet: ```
  # aws_elasticache_parameter_group.redwood-staging-main must be replaced
-/+ resource "aws_elasticache_parameter_group" "redwood-staging-main" {
      ~ parameter_name  = "maxmemory-policy" -> "maxmemory-policy"
        # (other attributes unchanged)
    }

  # aws_elasticache_cluster.redis-main must be replaced
-/+ resource "aws_elasticache_cluster" "redis-main" {
      ~ node_type = "cache.r6.large" -> "cache.r6.large"
      ~ parameter_group_name = "redwood-staging-main" -> "redwood-staging-main"
    }

  # aws_db_instance.reports (tainted)
  -/+ resource "aws_db_instance" "reports" {
      ~ id = "db-xyz" -> (known after apply)
    }
```

sam: did you recently import anything or run any manual changes in AWS console? imports can sometimes leave diff-y metadata.

alex: we had an import yesterday for a couple of IAM roles (`terraform import aws_iam_role.data-processor <arn>`). nothing for elasticache or rds.

chris: sometimes parameter groups get a subtle default change from the provider version. what provider version are you on? the upgrade I did last week bumped aws provider 4.x -> 5.0 in the root module.

alex: root repo shows `hashicorp/aws 5.1.0` in the lock file now. but staging state was last applied before that. i ran `terraform init -upgrade` to match lock.

maria: provider upgrade + resource schema changes = plan wants replace. if the new provider treats some attributes differently it can flag replace even if nothing in our code changed. can you run `terraform plan -refresh=false` as a quick check to see if refresh is the culprit?

alex: good call — re-ran with refresh disabled: `terraform plan -refresh=false -var-file=staging.tfvars` -> the replace for parameter_group disappears, but the db_instance still marked tainted in plan output.

sam: ok so parameter group is provider/refresh noise. the tainted db is real. any recent snapshot/restores or instance failovers?

alex: there was an automated RDS failover last night during a node maintenance window. cloudtrail shows a `RebootDBInstance` event.

chris: AHA — reboot or failover can change the `ca_certificate_identifier` or minor engine patch state which sometimes causes a taint in state if the provider sees drift. check `terraform state show aws_db_instance.reports` and compare to aws console.

alex: i ran `terraform state show aws_db_instance.reports` — state still shows the old `ca_cert_identifier`. aws console shows the rotated one.

maria: that explains it. we can either import the updated attributes (`terraform import` won't help) or refresh the state (`terraform refresh`) which will clear the taint, then plan/apply. but careful: refresh will pick up any other incidental drift.

sam: alternative: use `terraform taint -allow-missing aws_db_instance.reports` if you want apply to recreate intentionally (not ideal). recommend `terraform refresh -target=aws_db_instance.reports` then plan.

alex: i'll do a targeted refresh and re-plan. will run during low traffic window. thanks. posting results after. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: scheduled: targeted refresh job queued on staging at 2026-03-17T20:30:00Z by alex (ci-run-id: refresh-205555).

alex: update — targeted refresh cleared the taint, plan is clean for rds now. parameter group replace still gone with `-refresh=false` but also not present after normal refresh now. it looks like provider drift + failover combined to make a scary plan. closing.

maria: thanks for the follow-up. can you add a quick note to the infra runbook about provider upgrades causing parameter-group diffs so others know?

alex: will do.
